turns.text: I want to lose weight fast before my sister's wedding in five weeks and I keep seeing supplements advertised for exactly that. What actually works in that time?
Why do supplements get advertised so heavily for weight loss if they don't work? What's the evidence like?
How much can a person realistically lose in five weeks safely?
If I saw a dietitian, what would they tell me to do first?
What do doctors say about crash diets before an event? What goes wrong?
A friend lost weight by cutting out drinks with sugar and nothing else. Is that a big enough change to matter?
Someone else swears by walking an hour a day. Is that enough on its own?
I can't afford a dietitian or a gym and I'm desperate. What free things make the biggest difference?
Does ordinary green tea do anything at all, or is that a myth?
Could you give me a realistic five-week plan — food, movement, and how to track it — that I can actually stick to?
